lifestyle-health.title: Diabetes Remission in 90 Days? Doctors Explain What the Term Really Means
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Remission means an HbA1c below 6.5% held for at least three months without medication — a definition, not a deadline. Doctors explain the weight-loss mechanism, the South Asian risk caveat, and why real-world remission rates are far lower than trial headlines.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A person checks blood glucose with a finger-prick glucometer. Doctors say type 2 diabetes remission means an HbA1c below 6.5 percent sustained for at least three months without glucose-lowering medication.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians develop metabolic problems at lower BMI levels, doctors note, so diaspora readers should weigh waist size and lipids alongside weight when judging remission prospects.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: Losing 10-15% of body weight improves remission chances.
Excess abdominal fat complicates blood glucose regulation.

lifestyle-health.title: Traditional Indian Diet and Daily Walks Put 61% of Early Diabetes Patients in Remission, Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In a 87-person Maharashtra trial, a moderate-carbohydrate diet of everyday Indian foods plus a 40-minute daily walk produced an estimated 60.9% remission rate at six months — with walking consistency the strongest predictor. The researchers caution it was a single-arm study and no one should change medication without a doctor.

sources.label: PubMed — Diabetes and Metabolic Syndrome journal study abstract

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians develop Type 2 diabetes earlier and at lower weights; a remission programme built on everyday Indian food and walking, tested in Maharashtra, is directly relevant to diaspora readers in the first two years after diagnosis.

lifestyle-health.title: Overspent This Diwali? A Sober Plan to Clear Festive Card Debt
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Card debt at over 40% a year is the most expensive money in the house. Here is the order to tackle it: total it, pay above the minimum, then move what remains to cheaper money.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Diwali diyas and candles during the festival. Experts advise a sober plan to clear festive card debt after Diwali overspending.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Diaspora readers sending money home for Diwali face the same festive overspend in two currencies; the consolidation order and rate gap apply on both sides.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

steps.detail: List every card balance and BNPL due with its due date before deciding anything.
Set a target clearance date; the minimum due barely touches principal at 40%-plus annual charges.
A lower or teaser rate, or a transfer on EMI, works if you can clear it in the near future.
Personal loans start from about 10.99% a year; take the shortest tenure you can afford.
Bank FLCCs may help negotiate interest reductions or relief on punitive charges.
